display.purpose: The daily-allowance sentence only. 2rem phones, 2.75rem from 640px, 3.25rem from 1024px; max 24ch.

headline.purpose: Page titles, including the Overview greeting. 1.875rem phones, 2.25rem from 640px.

title.purpose: Section headings and fieldset legends; 1.25rem in dialog headers.

figure.purpose: Summary money amounts; 1.5rem phones, 1.75rem from 640px; always tabular.

body-sm.purpose: Explanatory text in ink-700, held to 60-62ch; table text.

label.purpose: Names above figures, captions, row metadata, in Pencil. Sentence case.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, bottom sheets and toasts. Never in-flow content.

motion.name: control-colour
motion.purpose: Background, border and colour changes on buttons and fields. State changes are otherwise instant.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All transitions and animations collapse under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Day grid goes from 8 to 16 columns; figures row from 2 to 4 columns; side padding 16px to 32px.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Forest rail replaces the header bar and bottom bar; two-column pages; worksheet panels gain a border.

focus.purpose: Every focusable element; fields use offset 0 and shift their border to forest-600.

fonts.note: Besley has no ₹ glyph; the serif stack falls back to Anek Latin for the rupee sign. Anek Latin is loaded with the wdth axis.

narrative.overview:
The pay cycle is drawn the way a doodhwala's monthly card is: a ruled grid of day boxes, each holding what that day took, today's box filled solid, and payday rubber-stamped at the end. Everything else in the system is ruled paper around that card. Surfaces are one warm paper ramp, text is charcoal ink, and a solid forest-green field holds the navigation like the cover of a ledger. The single loudest element on any screen that carries it is the daily-allowance sentence, set in a Clarendon-style serif with the rupee figure coloured inline.

Density is high but calm. Information sits in ruled rows and ruled cells rather than cards; a hairline in the paper ramp does the work that a box and a shadow would do elsewhere. Money is always set in tabular lining figures so columns line up. State changes are instant: a paid bill gets a stamp, not an animation.

The system rejects the category default of KPI tiles in a row with a donut chart, and the product's confirmed rejections apply: no purple-blue gradients, glowing blobs, glassmorphism, rounded cards around every element, emoji icons, or decorative charts.
keyCharacteristics: One stepped paper ramp supplies every neutral; no stray greys.
Forest green owns navigation, primary action, and "inside the plan".
Amber and red are status colours, rationed.
Ruled rows and ruled cells instead of cards; square or near-square corners (0-3px).
Besley serif for headings and the allowance sentence; Anek Latin for UI and every figure.
Tabular lining numerals on all money.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every neutral comes from paper-50 to paper-500 or ink-600 to ink-900. A grey from outside these steps is a defect.

rules.name: The Amber Is For Bills Rule
rules.body: Amber marks a bill that needs paying and nothing else. A day that went over its share is not amber; it gets a 2px charcoal top rule over its spent fill.

rules.name: The Red Means Short Rule
rules.body: Red marks money that is genuinely short, a bill that is overdue, or the system failing or destroying something. Never use red to mean "less than before" or "worse than the alternative".

rules.name: The Colour Plus Words Rule
rules.body: Status colour is never alone: every stamp carries a Lucide icon and words, every day-box notch is backed by the box's accessible description, and every over-share mark appears in the key.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every money amount, date numeral, and percentage in a column is set with tabular lining figures. A rupee amount in proportional figures is a defect.

rules.name: The One Big Number Rule
rules.body: Display scale belongs to the allowance sentence. Page titles stay at headline scale even when the page has nothing larger.

rules.name: The Paper Doesn't Float Rule
rules.body: In-flow content never carries a shadow. If something needs separation, give it a rule or step it one paper tone.

dos: Do take every neutral from the paper and ink ramps (paper-50 to paper-500, ink-600 to ink-900).
Do set every money figure in tabular lining numerals, with Indian digit grouping.
Do separate content with hairlines (paper-300) and card rules (paper-400) rather than boxes.
Do pair every status colour with words and a Lucide icon.
Do mark a day over its share with a 2px ink-900 top rule over the spent fill.
Do keep the allowance sentence the only display-scale text, with the figure coloured inline (forest-700 normally, red-800 when short).
Do keep corners at 0px for structure, 3px for controls, 2px for stamps.
Do make state changes instant; motion is limited to 120ms colour transitions and the chevron on "How this is worked out", and is removed under reduced motion.
Do write UI copy as plain statements with real figures ("You have ₹43 a day until payday."), never scolding about spending and never using SaaS slogans such as "unlock" or "supercharge".
donts: Don't use amber for anything except bills that are due.
Don't use red for "worse than before" or a less favourable comparison; red is for real shortfalls, overdue bills, and system errors or destructive actions.
Don't wrap sections in rounded, shadowed cards; the only bordered panels are the square worksheet panel and dialogs.
Don't put a shadow on anything in the page flow.
Don't show a positive allowance when nothing is safe to spend.
Don't let the day grid scroll sideways, or shrink boxes below 40px to fit more columns.
Don't use KPI tiles in a row or a donut chart for the cycle summary.
Don't use emoji or glyph icons; icons are Lucide line icons.
